What the members of a class disagree about

Source: R/class_members.R
mc_class_coefficients.Rd

Fits the directed layer on the residual covariance of a fit under every member of a Markov equivalence class and collects, for each arc, the values of its structural coefficient that the class allows. The coefficients are those of the closed-form root, mc_dag_closed_root, and the standardized ones are \(\gamma^*_{jk}=\gamma_{jk}(\Sigma_{b,kk}/ \Sigma_{b,jj})^{1/2}\), as in mc_dag_coefficients, with \(j\) the child and \(k\) the parent. An arc whose values coincide across members is one whose coefficient the class determines; an arc whose values move is one for which a single number would report a choice the data did not make.

Usage

mc_class_coefficients(fit, cpdag = NULL, max_members = 1000L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mcg_class_coef'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph", whose residual covariance the layer is fitted to.

cpdag

the class, as an adjacency matrix or an "mcg_cpdag" object; NULL runs mc_graph_pipeline on the fit.

max_members

cap on the number of members enumerated, as in mc_class_members.

...

passed to mc_graph_pipeline when cpdag is NULL; ignored by the print method.

x

an object of class "mcg_class_coef".

Value

An object of class "mcg_class_coef": a list with arcs, a data frame with one row per arc present in some member (from, to, parent, child, the number of members that contain it n_members, the range of its coefficient gamma_min, gamma_max and of its standardized coefficient gamma_std_min, gamma_std_max, and the logical common, true when no undirected edge of the class touches the head of the arc); members, the list of DAGs; values, the per-member table of coefficients (member, from, to, gamma, gamma_std); n_members; truncated, whether the enumeration was capped; and response_names. The print method returns x invisibly. An error is raised when the class has no consistent extension.

What the values are

Every member reproduces the same fitted covariance when the class is a CPDAG, and the second moments do not distinguish among them. The direction of a compelled arc is a property of the class, but its coefficient is a partial regression coefficient given the other parents of its head, and those can change from one member to another. The values are coefficients of linear projections of Pearson residuals. Enumerating a quantity over the members of a class follows Maathuis, Kalisch and Buehlmann (2009), who apply it to intervention effects; the coefficients reported here admit that reading only under causal assumptions the procedure does not check: a linear structural model with independent innovations whose graph belongs to the class, causal sufficiency and absence of selection bias.

Which arcs the class pins down

An arc has the same coefficient in every member whose parent set for its head is the same. That happens for every member when no undirected edge of the CPDAG touches the head of the arc, which is the condition to check before reporting a single value. The returned table flags it in common.

References

Maathuis, M. H., Kalisch, M. and Buehlmann, P. (2009). Estimating high-dimensional intervention effects from observational data. The Annals of Statistics 37(6A), 3133-3164. doi:10.1214/09-AOS685

See also

mc_class_members, mc_dag_closed_root

Other equivalence class: mc_class_members(), mc_sid()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 400; x <- rnorm(n)
z1 <- rnorm(n); z2 <- rnorm(n); z3 <- 0.7 * z1 + 0.7 * z2 + rnorm(n)
d <- data.frame(y1 = z1, y2 = z2, y3 = z3, x = x)
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1 ~ x, y2 ~ x, y3 ~ x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
mc_class_coefficients(f)
#> Coefficients over the 1 member of the class
#> An arc marked common has the same value in every member.
#> 
#>   parent child n_members gamma_min gamma_max gamma_std_min gamma_std_max common
#> 1     y1    y3         1     0.559     0.559         0.560         0.560   TRUE
#> 2     y2    y3         1     0.496     0.496         0.497         0.497   TRUE
# }
